description: Curated classification of every item of the reference material and the methodology rules the engine implements. Rules cite the items they were derived from. No exercise numbers here are used for calculation.

sources.exercise_docx: Exercise document (workshop 1): problem statement a)–g), activity-on-arrow figure, three-point estimate table and PERT formula images.
sources.concepts_xlsx: General concepts workbook: sheets 'Diagrama Gantt (2)', 'Diagrama Gantt', 'Red Actividad Nodo', 'PERT Probabilístico', 'CPM', 'Problema 2 CPM', 'Hoja1'. Content is almost entirely pasted images; there are no live formulas.

pert_expected_time.statement: Expected activity time for the beta (three-estimate) distribution.

pert_activity_variance.statement: Activity variance for the three-estimate distribution.

project_variance.statement: Variance of the expected project time = sum of the variances of the activities on the critical path ('Sumatorio total de las actividades críticas').
project_variance.note: The material only shows single-critical-path cases; with several critical paths the engine uses the path of largest variance by default (option: sum all critical activities) and reports every path.

standardization.statement: Z = (predetermined time − expected minimum project time) / standard deviation of the expected minimum project time; P(T ≤ T_p) = Φ(Z).

probability_table_convention.statement: Worked examples round Z to two decimals and read Φ(Z) from a four-decimal normal table (e.g. Z = 1.6036 is used as 1.60, Φ = 0.9452).

percentile_convention.statement: For a target probability, take from the table the Z whose Φ reaches it (Z = 1.29 for 0.90), compute T_p = t_e + Z·σ, and round up to the next whole time unit when whole units are required.

four_significant_times.statement: Earliest start (as soon as precedences allow), latest start (without altering the minimum project duration), earliest finish, latest finish.

slack.statement: Slack (holgura) is the maximum delay of an activity without altering the minimum project duration; zero-slack activities are critical.

project_duration_multiple_terminals.statement: With several terminal activities the minimum project time is the largest earliest finish among them.

gantt_layout.statement: Double-entry table: activities in rows, elapsed time units in columns. Two rows per activity: first row bars start as early as possible respecting precedence (ES→EF); second row bars start as late as possible without delaying the project (LS→LF). An 'Observaciones' column marks 'Actividad Crítica' (shaded) or 'Holgura de N semanas'.

aon_preferred.statement: Of the two representations (ACTIVIDAD-RAMAL: activities on arcs, nodes are events; ACTIVIDAD-NODO: activities on nodes, arcs are precedences) the material uses ACTIVIDAD-NODO (Bernard Roy method).

aon_node_notation.statement: Node = circle split into cells: activity name | activity duration; earliest start | earliest finish; latest start | latest finish; slack at the bottom. Critical nodes are shaded and critical arcs drawn as double lines.

aoa_to_aon.statement: Exercise figures may be activity-on-arrow networks (numbered event nodes, lettered arrows, dashed dummy 'ficticia' arrows). Precedences are read off the arrow network first — an activity follows every activity entering its start node, including those carried by dummy arrows — and the ACTIVIDAD-NODO network is drawn from them.

crash_slope.statement: Direct-cost increase per time unit of reduction; an activity with Dn = Dc has no slope (cannot be shortened).

crashing_procedure.statement: Compute the critical path and normal direct cost; shorten, one time unit at a time, the critical activity with the smallest slope; recompute (the critical path may change); with several critical paths shorten all of them simultaneously using the cheapest combination (an activity shared by the paths can be cheaper than one activity per path); stop when a critical path has all its activities at minimum duration or the owner's required time is reached.

total_cost_optimum.statement: Total cost per duration = direct + indirect cost; the recommended duration is the one with minimum total cost.

cells.summary: Title: project administration Gantt - PERT - CPM.
Introduction: basic tools are the Gantt chart, probabilistic PERT and CPM.
Direct cost examples (I3:I8): raw material, labour, transport, commissions, advertising.
Indirect cost examples (K4:K7): energy, indirect labour, administrative staff.
Main uses (B10:B16): minimum project duration, probability of finishing by a predetermined time, bottleneck/critical activities.
First step is representing the project as a network; the Gantt chart helps identify the times.
ACTIVIDAD-RAMAL vs ACTIVIDAD-NODO; the material uses ACTIVIDAD-NODO for easier representation of activities and precedences.
